name: personal_research_assistant_rag_eval_v1
description: Starter RAG retrieval-evaluation dataset for the AWS Personal Research Assistant MVP. Fill relevant_chunk_ids after indexing, using the chunk/document IDs returned by your retriever.
id_field_note: Use relevant_chunk_ids for exact recall/precision. source_files and expected_sections are included to help label the ground truth.

items.question: What is the current AWS deployment path for the RAG MVP?
items.expected_answer_summary: Browser/API path using Cognito, API Gateway/Lambda/FastAPI, guardrails, retrieval, Bedrock embeddings, FAISS in S3, Bedrock model routing, S3 memory, CloudWatch, optional LangSmith.

items.question: How does the retrieval pipeline combine BM25 and vector search?
items.expected_answer_summary: BM25 and vector search run, results are merged, deterministically reranked, and top results are passed to the LLM.

items.question: What are the default top_k and LLM context size for retrieval?
items.expected_answer_summary: The system retrieves up to top_k=25 candidates by default and sends the top 5 reranked chunks to the LLM.

items.question: Why does the MVP use deterministic chunking instead of LLM-based chunking?
items.expected_answer_summary: Deterministic chunking is fixed, reproducible, testable, predictable for costs, and avoids hidden variability.

items.question: What chunking strategies are attempted before sliding-window fallback?
items.expected_answer_summary: Whole-document, section-aware, paragraph-aware, sentence-aware, deterministic semantic chunking, then sliding-window fallback.

items.question: How does chat history work in the current MVP?
items.expected_answer_summary: The workflow loads prior messages by session_id, retrieves, routes/generates, then saves user and assistant messages.

items.question: What are the current limitations of chat history?
expected_sections: What Is Not Yet First-Class History
items.expected_answer_summary: It lacks structured timestamps, citations, retrieval scores, hallucination metadata, selected model, searchable history, and conversation-management UX.

items.question: What guardrails run before and after the LLM call?
items.expected_answer_summary: A deterministic prompt guardrail runs before retrieval/LLM, and a grounding-risk policy runs after generation.

items.question: What happens when grounding risk is high?
items.expected_answer_summary: The policy can expose low-confidence metadata, escalate the answer, or return a safe fallback for very high risk.

items.question: What are the main cost drivers for the MVP?
items.expected_answer_summary: Generation tokens, embedding tokens, API/Lambda volume, Cognito MAUs/MFA, S3, and CloudWatch.

items.question: Which application paths are most expensive and why?
items.expected_answer_summary: Chat and upload are the most expensive because they fan out into retrieval/model calls and parsing/embedding/indexing.

items.question: What does the CloudWatch cost dashboard show?
items.expected_answer_summary: Request volume, Lambda invocations/errors, API 4xx/5xx, latency, throttles, and integration latency.

items.question: What metadata is sent to LangSmith?
items.expected_answer_summary: Metadata-first traces including retrieval counts/scores, selected model, routing reason, hallucination score/action, token estimates, cost, and latency signals.

items.question: How is the LangSmith API key handled in AWS?
items.expected_answer_summary: The key is stored in AWS Secrets Manager and read by Lambda at runtime; it is not stored in GitHub or plain environment variables.

items.question: What rate limits are applied to chat and upload routes?
items.expected_answer_summary: Chat is limited per Cognito sub, uploads are limited per Cognito sub, and auth config is limited by client IP/X-Forwarded-For.

items.question: Why is the current rate limiter not a full production quota system?
items.expected_answer_summary: It is process-local and in-memory, so separate Lambda execution environments have separate counters.

items.question: What vector store does the deployed MVP currently use?
items.expected_answer_summary: Bedrock Titan embeddings feed a FAISS vector store, with the FAISS index persisted in S3.

items.question: Why was OpenSearch Serverless removed from the MVP deployment?
items.expected_answer_summary: It was removed to avoid ongoing OpenSearch Serverless collection charges during MVP testing.

items.question: When should the MVP move from Lambda to ECS Fargate?
items.expected_answer_summary: When uploads, indexing, longer calls, concurrency, retries, cold starts, or heavier parsing make synchronous Lambda brittle.

items.question: What role would SQS play in the enterprise architecture?
items.expected_answer_summary: SQS decouples uploads from background document processing, allowing workers to chunk, embed, index, and update status asynchronously.

items.question: When would AgentCore become useful for this assistant?
items.expected_answer_summary: AgentCore helps when the assistant needs governed tool use, multi-step actions, structured memory, evaluation, audit trails, and controlled tool access.

items.question: How does GitHub OIDC avoid storing AWS access keys?
items.expected_answer_summary: GitHub issues a short-lived OIDC token that AWS validates, allowing the workflow to assume a dedicated deployment role without storing long-lived AWS keys.

items.question: How should web access be added without confusing users?
items.expected_answer_summary: Use private sources first, allow bounded web fallback only when justified, and clearly label answer origin.

items.question: What are the main risks of adding web access?
items.expected_answer_summary: User confusion, product drift, higher latency, higher token use, more hallucination surface, and privacy/compliance concerns.

items.question: What should the enterprise architecture use for metadata and entitlements?
items.expected_answer_summary: DynamoDB or Postgres should store metadata, entitlements, usage, and related application records.
